I'm 42, been farming these 8 mu since I was 17 when my father got too old for the heavy work. My family has seven people — my wife, my parents, my two children, and my younger brother. Me and my brother do construction work in Handan city when there's no urgent farm work, which brings in cash but also means we're short of hands during busy times.

It's early October now, time to plant winter wheat. I farm all 8 mu in wheat-maize rotation — that's the only way to feed everyone and have some grain to sell. I don't have money to try fancy things; every decision is about making sure we have enough to eat and maybe a little profit.

For wheat, I'll plant around October 10th. I buy the improved seed from the shop in town, about 15 jin per mu, costs 25 yuan. I used to save my own seed but the yield got worse year after year. The seed shop variety gives me about 400 jin per mu when the weather is normal.

Fertilizer is my biggest worry. I put down about 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — when I plant. That costs about 1.2 yuan per jin. Then at jointing time in spring, I topdress with about 30 jin per mu of urea. My neighbor Lao Wang cut back on urea last year to save money for his son's wedding, and his wheat was noticeably shorter. I can't take that risk with seven mouths to feed. So I'll stick with what I did last year — roughly the same amount. I don't buy separate phosphate or potash; whatever is in the compound fertilizer is enough for my land.

Irrigation... I have the tube well, but pumping costs electricity money. I'll irrigate three times for wheat: once right after planting if the soil is dry, once at jointing in late March, and once when the grain is filling. Three times has always been enough for me. Some people do four, but that's too expensive.

For pests, I spray herbicide once in early spring for the weeds. I also keep insecticide in the shed — last year there were aphids and I had to spray. I'll watch for them this year too.

The real headache is always June. We harvest wheat around June 8-10 with a hired combine — 50 yuan per mu — and then I have maybe five days at most to get the maize in the ground. I hire a tractor with a maize planter, 30 yuan per mu, because planting 8 mu by hand in three days is impossible. For maize seed, I buy hybrid seed every year — about 3 jin per mu, 40 yuan. You can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work.

For maize fertilizer, I put down 100 jin per mu of compound at planting. Then at the big trumpet stage — that's when the plants are tall and growing fast — I spread about 25 jin of urea per mu. Last year I skipped the topdressing to save money because my daughter needed school fees, and the maize yield was a bit lower. This year I'll do both.

Maize irrigation depends on the summer rain. If July is dry, I irrigate once at flowering. If it's very dry, maybe twice. But usually once is enough. I spray herbicide right after planting, and if I see armyworm, I'll spray insecticide.

For labor, my wife and my father help with most things. My mother looks after the children. During the June rush, if my brother is away working, I'll hire two or three people for a couple days to help with the harvest and planting. That costs 120 yuan per day per person. For wheat harvest, the combine does the cutting but we still need to bag and carry the grain home.

I expect about 400 kg per mu for wheat and maybe 450 kg per mu for maize. That's not great but it's stable. With wheat price around 2.4 yuan per kg and maize around 2.2 yuan, I can make some money after costs. My total spending on seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation, machinery hire, and hired labor will be about 5,000-plus yuan. That's a lot of money for us, but my brother's construction work helps cover it.
